relationship: Transmitting a frame with selectable parity and faults connects error detection to ACK/NAK and ARQ retransmission.

learnerLoop.action: Set the message and parity options, introduce noise if desired, then transmit.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The data frame, received frame and acknowledgement state change.
learnerLoop.evidence: Frame views, decoded text and result panel show detection and any resend.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Change the error pattern or protocol option and predict the reply.

invariants: Displayed parity and reply evidence derive from the transmitted frame and chosen scheme.
An ARQ resend follows the lab's visible acknowledgement state.
safeAdaptations: Change messages, noise examples or prompts while preserving data-frame, check and reply causality.
nonGoals: Providing real error correction or a live communications protocol.

task.description: Test detectable and undetectable transmission errors, then inspect ARQ response.
task.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

model.description: Baseline-aligned source/channel/receiver matrices beneath the DATA/reply track.
model.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

settings.description: Message/parity choices, bit error controls and optional lost reply.
settings.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

evidence.description: Horizontal transmission strip above the three columns: current transfer, receiver verdict, decoded/original comparison and ARQ consequences.
evidence.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

frame.domain: Seven ASCII data bits plus row parity; block mode adds column parity for groups up to eight characters.

errors.domain: Data, row parity and optional column parity bits.
errors.source: Generated editable channel cells or Flip one random bit.

reply.source: Parity outcome and Lose next reply.

modes.parity: Row parity or block parity, even or odd.
modes.channel: Only the channel copy is editable; sender parity is fixed at message preparation.

dependencies: Transmit is disabled during a running exchange.
Detected parity failure gives NAK; loss of reply causes timeout.
ARQ retransmits the original frame, while undetected corruption produces ACK and no error-driven resend.
implementation.completion: Each exchange ends in acceptance, detected error, or timeout; eligible ARQ resend ends with recovery evidence.
limitations: Parity detects some error patterns but cannot guarantee unchanged data.
Maximum sixteen printable characters, split into teaching blocks of at most eight.
